correctness.rationale: Affine section geometry gives \(F=q^{-1/2}-s^2q^{-3/2}\). The exact two-Gram calculation has \(\mathrm{tr}=S\) and \(\det=(4/45)D\); the best rank-one residual is the smaller squared singular value. Strict Cauchy–Schwarz characterizes balls. Sphere fourth moments give the exact \(1/24\) traceless quadratic coefficient; direct axial integral recurrences plus dominated convergence prove the nonzero prolate constant and vanishing logarithmic oblate defect. The new theorem is therefore neither a mere corollary of the named prior claims nor a known table recomputation, although it uses standard singular-value theory.
